notes: An Octopus Card works for everything (MTR, trams, ferries, shops); buy one at the airport. The Airport Express takes 24 minutes.
Summers are humid at 33°C, and typhoon warnings are possible (everything closes at Signal 8). Sightsee in the morning and head to malls or museums in the afternoon.
Dim sum is eaten in the morning and at lunchtime. Queues are normal at cheap Michelin-listed places like Tim Ho Wan and Kam's Roast Goose.
Tipping is not expected, as a 10% service charge is added. Cash is still common; small restaurants don't take cards.
The Star Ferry and the Peak Tram are Hong Kong rituals. Go up to the Peak at 08:00, and return at 19:00 for the evening lights.
Bring your passport for Macau. Ferries to Lamma and Cheung Chau leave from Central Piers 4 and 5.

transit.name: Octopus Card
transit.why_chosen: It works on the MTR, trams, buses, the Star Ferry and in shops, so it is useful everywhere in Hong Kong.

stops.name: Peak Tram
stops.tips: The first trams at 07:30 have no queue. It takes 8 minutes to reach Victoria Peak; around 88 HKD return.

stops.name: Victoria Peak Sky Terrace 428
stops.tips: The terrace at the summit has 360° views of the harbour, and the morning haze clears.

stops.name: Peak Circle Walk
stops.tips: A flat 3.5 km walk around the summit, shaded and scenic.

stops.name: Tim Ho Wan Central
stops.tips: The world's cheapest Michelin-starred dim sum. Don't miss the BBQ pork buns (char siu bao).

stops.name: Central-Mid-Levels Escalator
stops.tips: The world's longest outdoor covered escalator system, leading up to SoHo and Tai Kwun.

backups.name: Lan Fong Yuen
backups.tips: A cha chaan teng (Hong Kong tea café) since 1952. Try the milk tea and the pork chop sandwich.

backups.name: Tai Kwun
backups.tips: A former police station and prison, now a free cultural centre.

stops.name: Star Ferry Central Pier
stops.tips: The legendary 8-minute ferry from Central to Tsim Sha Tsui. It costs 5 HKD with an Octopus card.

stops.name: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade
stops.tips: The Avenue of Stars and harbour views. Good for morning photos.

stops.name: Hong Kong Museum of Art
stops.tips: A harbourfront art museum with free entry, showing Chinese calligraphy and contemporary art.

stops.name: Mak's Noodle Jordan
stops.tips: A wonton noodle classic. The bowls are small, so order two.

stops.name: Temple Street Night Market
stops.tips: Fortune tellers, street food and cheap goods. It comes alive after 18:00; try the claypot rice.

backups.name: Australia Dairy Company
backups.tips: Egg sandwiches on toast and steamed milk pudding. The queue moves fast.

backups.name: Kowloon Park
backups.tips: A park in Tsim Sha Tsui with flamingos. A swap for the museum.

stops.name: Ngong Ping 360 Cable Car
stops.tips: A 25-minute cable car ride from Tung Chung (around 300 HKD return; glass-bottom cabins cost extra), with views of sea and mountains.

stops.name: Tian Tan Buddha
stops.tips: A 34 m bronze Buddha. Climb the 268 steps for views over Lantau.

stops.name: Po Lin Monastery
stops.tips: The monastery at the foot of the Buddha. Vegetarian meal tickets are sold here.

stops.name: Po Lin Vegetarian Restaurant
stops.tips: The monastery's vegetarian kitchen: simple and good.

stops.name: Tai O Fishing Village
stops.tips: A village of stilt houses. A boat tour (with a chance of pink dolphins) costs 30 HKD, and there is a dried fish market.

backups.name: Tai O Dried Seafood Market
backups.tips: Grilled seafood in Tai O. A swap for the monastery.

backups.name: Cheung Sha Beach
backups.tips: Lantau's long beach, good for swimming in summer.

days.theme: Mong Kok and Sham Shui Po

stops.name: Chi Lin Nunnery
stops.tips: A Tang-style wooden nunnery built without nails, with lotus ponds.

stops.name: Nan Lian Garden
stops.tips: A Chinese garden opposite the nunnery, with a golden pagoda.

stops.name: Wong Tai Sin Temple
stops.tips: Fortune sticks (kau cim) and incense. It is Hong Kong's busiest temple.

stops.name: Kwan Kee Bamboo Noodle
stops.tips: In Sham Shui Po, noodles kneaded with a bamboo pole. A legend.

stops.name: Apliu Street, Sham Shui Po
stops.tips: An electronics and fabric market in Hong Kong's most local neighbourhood, with street food.

backups.name: Tim Ho Wan Sham Shui Po
backups.tips: The original Tim Ho Wan branch.

stops.name: Repulse Bay Beach
stops.tips: A sandy beach on the south of the island. Sun loungers are free, there are showers, and mornings are quiet.

stops.name: Stanley Market
stops.tips: A market in a seaside town, selling silk and souvenirs.

stops.name: The Boathouse Stanley
stops.tips: Seafood on the Stanley waterfront, with a terrace.

stops.name: Stanley Promenade
stops.tips: Murray House and the waterfront. Stop for coffee.

stops.name: Shek O Beach
stops.tips: A village beach, good for a sunset swim.

backups.name: Deep Water Bay
backups.tips: A quieter cove next to Repulse Bay.

stops.name: Yung Shue Wan Lamma
stops.tips: A 30-minute ferry from Central. A car-free island village with cafés.

stops.name: Lamma Family Trail
stops.tips: A 1.5-hour coastal walk from Yung Shue Wan to Sok Kwu Wan, with a stop at Hung Shing Yeh beach.

stops.name: Hung Shing Yeh Beach
stops.tips: Lamma's swimming beach, with showers and a snack bar.

stops.name: Rainbow Seafood Lamma
stops.tips: Seafood in Sok Kwu Wan, with a free ferry back to Central.

stops.name: Sok Kwu Wan Pier
stops.tips: Fish farms and the return ferry.

backups.name: Cheung Chau Island
backups.tips: An alternative island, good for cycling and beaches.

stops.name: Hong Kong Park
stops.tips: A park among the skyscrapers, with an aviary and a lake.

stops.name: Ding Ding Tram Line
stops.tips: Ride the historic double-decker tram to Wan Chai. Take a front seat upstairs; the fare is 3 HKD.

stops.name: Kam's Roast Goose Wan Chai
stops.tips: Michelin-starred roast goose for a farewell lunch. Expect a 30-minute queue.

stops.name: Airport Express Hong Kong Station
stops.tips: The airport train takes 24 minutes, with in-town check-in.

backups.name: Joy Hing Roasted Meat
backups.tips: Cheap char siu in Wan Chai.

backups.name: Blue House Wan Chai
backups.tips: A historic blue building and neighbourhood museum. A swap for the tram.
